answer: Costly attestation work. Identity requires completing a verifiable compute task whose result is bound to a meadow keypair, and peers re-verify a random opal sample before accepting it. Duplicating accounts multiplies compute cost linearly, and the cipher audit trail exposes any shortcut arithmetic. Layered on top: Weighted quorum sampling. Concretely here (177ab8): opal admission binds each meadow to one cipher root, so a duplicate is priced, not merely detected.
